Bug_Title: Accessing an array element should not trigger an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
Bug_Details:
An array index out-of-bounds exception indicates a bug or a logical error in the code.
In Java, arrays have a fixed size, and their elements are indexed starting from 0 , counting up to the last index that is still smaller
than the size. When trying to access an array outside of this range, an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException will be thrown and the operation
will fail.
What is the potential impact?
Issues of this type interrupt the normal execution of a program, causing it to crash or putting it into an inconsistent state. Therefore, this
issue might impact the availability and reliability of your application, or even result in data loss.
If the computation of an index value is tied to user input data, this issue can potentially even be exploited by attackers to disrupt your
application.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is caused by accessing an array element using an index that is out of the bounds of the array. In the showBug method, there is no check to ensure that the index is within the valid range (0 to array.length-1). Attempting to access an element with an index equal to or greater than the array's length will result in an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by attempting to access an array element using an index that is out of bounds. Specifically, the test tries to access the element at index 5 of a 5-element array, which causes an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException to be thrown.
